# nginxproxymanager_custom_certificate

Custom certificates do not support updates, therefore the recommended way of updating a certificate is to taint the Terraform resource to force re-creation.

## Example Usage 

```terraform
resource "tls_private_key" "example" {
  algorithm = "ECDSA"
}

resource "tls_self_signed_cert" "example" {
  key_algorithm         = tls_private_key.example.algorithm
  private_key_pem       = tls_private_key.example.private_key_pem
  validity_period_hours = 24 * 365
  allowed_uses = [
    "server_auth",
  ]

  dns_names = ["test.domain.com"]

  subject {
    common_name  = "test.domain.com"
    organization = "ACME Examples, Inc"
  }
}

resource "nginxproxymanager_custom_certificate" "example" {
  nice_name       = "test.domain.com"
  certificate     = tls_self_signed_cert.example.cert_pem
  certificate_key = tls_private_key.example.private_key_pem
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate` (String) Body of the certificate in PEM format.
- `certificate_key` (String, Sensitive) Private key of the certificate in PEM format.

### Optional

- `intermediate_certificate` (String) Intermediate certificate in the chain.
- `nice_name` (String) Nice name for the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the certificate.

```terraform
terraform import nginxproxymanager_custom_certificate 123
```
